claim: Pieverse ran from around 12 cents to 2 dollars in under a year, and the token is priced way ahead of the numbers the product publishes: it does not publish how many agents are running, how many subscribers pay, or its revenue.
why_this_claim: It is the video's own thesis (the CH6 read) and it stands alone on three things that are all inside the short: the price move plus Mike's disclosure (the hook), what the product is in one line (you rent an agent by the month), and the missing number (how many agents are running, not published, said with its 'not anywhere I checked' limit). It needs no chart, no supply math and no spoken figure beyond the hook's own, so nothing the captions print can disagree with a card. Three of the four gated FACE windows carry it, so the build is two native-vertical rebuilds.

assembled_read: Pieverse went from around 12 cents to $2 in under a year. And it is one of my plays, and I did the homework on exactly what it is. You rent an agent by the month. How many agents are actually running? Pieverse doesn't publish an agent count, a subscriber count, or revenue, at least not anywhere I checked. So here's my read. Pieverse is a live product with real backers and is priced way ahead of the numbers it publishes.

rejected.reason: The first half of the F4 face line, 'And what I couldn't find was the numbers that matters the most, right?'. It is the natural setup, but with it the spans run 31.4 s; captions would also print the take's 'numbers that matters'. Span 2 does the setup job in 1.76 s.

D1, 'The short version, Pieverse lets you rent an agent that has its own crypto wallet, and you talk to it inside an app, like Line or Kakao.' The fuller 'what it is' line, but 9.2 s; it opens inside the F1-out film burn and ends 0.15 s before the screen-share window (19.19) inside that edge's burn. The only in-silence exit is mid-sentence at 'wallet,' (15.04-15.44). Over budget either way.
'Here's how the product works.' ahead of span 2: adds 1.5 s for no new information and pushes the spans to 28.8 s.
Screen-share window (hard rule), and the voice says a fully diluted value of 1.7 billion while card D9 prints 1.78B.

The Skill Store counter lines (around 74,000 skills, 25,000 merchants, imported from ClawHub, 30 native, one paid install). Strong proof, but it is a second idea, runs 23 s as a unit, and the counter line cannot air without the import line (SCREENPLAY warning box 1).

Ending span 3 at 'or revenue,' (a cut in the 0.57 s silence 152.25-152.82) would clear the title-card flip and save 1.8 s, but it drops 'at least not anywhere I checked', the limit the screenplay says the line must keep. Kept.

risks: DELIVERY NOT HEARD. I worked from the transcript, the audio envelope and stills, not by listening. Two cold starts are inferred from the silences around them: 'You rent an agent by the month.' (0.50 s of silence after 'month.', but in the longform the next line continues the thought, so the pitch may not fall) and 'How many agents are actually running?' (the second half of the F4 take, 0.49 s of silence before it). If span 2 sounds unfinished, drop it: spans 1, 3, 4 total 25.56 s, still inside the lane's 24 to 28, and the build shrinks to the D5 card alone.

TRANSITION WINDOWS, three spans. Every face edge in this video sits at the centre of a 0.76 s film burn and the face takes fill their windows (pad 0), so spans 1 and 4 cannot leave or enter a face window outside a burn. I kept each cut on a FACE frame (checked on stills: his face under a warm wash at 9.63, 358.67, 366.30), which should read as a seam flash. Span 3 ends under the CH4 title-card flip of the 16:9 master (starts 154.08), because the flip begins under the last syllable of 'checked.'; it stays out of the short only if the native-vertical D5 card holds to the span end (the COVER-PLAN D5 beat covers it, 148.16-156.06 final). If the flip shows at the final QA, the fix is the overlay window, not the cut.

SPAN 3 IS MIXED (2.02 s face, then 6.19 s card) and labelled FACE so the painter crops the opening on his face. I read in short_spans_from_16x9.py that the label drives the crop; the face detector will find no face on the card frames, which should not matter because those frames are covered by the D5 card. In F4 his face sits right of frame centre and his raised hand at the left edge is cut by the 608 px crop (cosmetic).

The says fields in this plan already use the corrected spelling; every other word is as transcribed. Whisper prints the hook's figure as '$2'; AS-RECORDED says on-screen text carries no dollar sign, so confirm how the caption prints it. 'and is priced' (364.00) is kept as heard.

HOOK FIGURE. The take says 'to $2' where the script had 'to over 2 dollars' (all-time high 2.23, 1.78 at the recording). It is not on Mike's list of wrong spoken numbers and it is the longform's own open, so I used it; flagged in case he wants it judged by the same rule.

CARD TEXT THE SHORT NEVER SAYS. D5's left half prints 74,195 skills and 25,233 merchants. The short does not say the import caveat, so the vertical rebuild should keep that half at rest and lead with the NOT PUBLISHED half (SCREENPLAY warning box 1: those counters are never traction). C1's lit node prints '10 to 279 USD a month', a verified plan range the voice does not say in this span.
C1 IS ON SCREEN 1.76 s. Long enough for a caption and one lit node, short for a system-design diagram reflowed to 9:16. It is one of the two rebuilds; the agent-lit state alone is enough.
